mhc_export.assay__comments: The responses in this assay are expressed as % (cpm) of <sup>125</sup>I-β<sub>2</sub>m incorporation in the complex with peptide and HLA-B*1402 as analyzed by HPLC gel filtration. Values over 5% indicate specific binding.
mhc_export.reference__title: The HLA-B14 peptide binding site can accommodate peptides with different combinations of anchor residues.
mhc_export.epitope__comments: This peptide was synthesized based on the results obtained by sequencing endogenous HLA-B*1402 presented peptides. This is an alternate possible sequence for the peptide DAYRRIHSLA, since both A and R residues were identified for position 2 at equimolar amounts. At the moment of its publication, no matches could be found in the protein sequence databases, but at the moment of this data entry, this peptide has a match in a T-cell receptor alpha chain-c6.1A fusion protein isolated from a ataxia telangiectasia patient. Peptide DAYRRIHSLA has a match in the WT sequence for protein C6.1A.

mhc_export.epitope__comments: This peptide is said to correspond to residues 217-225 of the Nucleoprotein from Influenza A/Japan/305, but the corresponding sequence found in that protein has a I residue at position 225 instead of a T. It is predicted to bind HLA-B14 molecules based on the presence of 3 out of 5 conserved anchor residues for that MHC allele. An internal database source is provided here to account for the lack of agreement between the NP sequences present in the current protein databases and the author provided sequence.
